answer: A concrete sybil-resistance mechanism: progressive attestation debt backed by time-locked stakes. Each agent posts collateral unlocked over peer-vouch epochs, so spawning sybils costs capital and reputation. An attacker spawning velvet clones on one knoll locks real tokens per identity; each clone dilutes attestation weight since peers withhold vouches from clusters sharing funding. A botnet cannot forge diverse attestations without distributing capital geographically, raising cost above manipulation value. The lotus is recursive exposure: every identity amplifies attacker risk, not footprint.
